senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced.) lofty; ruler, lord; proud, haughty.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 113b:10">Pes. 113ᵇ</cite> <he>דל ג׳</he> a proud pauper.—Pl. <cite ref="C00020"><he>גֵּאִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="C00020"><he>גֵּיאִים</he></cite>.

Gen. R. s. 63 (ref. to גיים, Gen. XXV, 23) שני גֵיאֵי גוים וכ׳ two rulers of nations (Rome and Israel); Ber. 57ᵇ; Ab. Zar. 11ᵃ אל תקרי גוים אלא גֵּיִים read the word גיים not goyim (as the Masorah intimates) but geyim (lords); (Ms. M. a.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 110:21">Yalk. Gen. 110</cite> <cite ref="C00020"><he>גֵּאִים</he></cite>). Sifra B’ḥuck. Par. 2, ch. V (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 26:19">Lev. XXVI, 19</cite>) <he>אלו הג׳ וכ׳</he> the ‘pride of your power’, those are the lordly (patrons) of whom Israel is proud.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:10:4">Cant. R. to III, 10</cite> <he>ארבע ג׳ הם גאה וכ׳</he> there are four majestic rulers (in the animal kingdom) the ruler among birds &c.; <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 23:13">Ex. R. s. 23</cite>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 13b:5">Ḥag. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>שמתגאה על הג׳</he> who is exalted (rules) over the rulers.—Y. Kidd. IV, end, 66ᶜ. <he>רובן של עבדים ג׳</he> most slaves (when raised to power) are overbearing; <cite ref="Tractate Soferim 15:10">Treat. Sof’rim XV, 10</cite> <cite ref="N00019"><he>נאים</he></cite> (corr. acc.); a. fr.—V. <cite ref="C00020"><he>גֵּאִים</he></cite>.
